title: Integral rho section modules are nonzero finite free rational representations
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and algebraically closed residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams over this base. Suppose $H$ is split semisimple simply connected: its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, every central isogeny onto such a fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, and choose a split maximal torus $T\subseteq H$ and a Borel subgroup scheme $B\supseteq T$. Here a central isogeny is a surjective group homomorphism with finite central kernel; solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial; a split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; maximal tori and Borel subgroup schemes have, on each geometric fibre, a maximal torus and a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, respectively. Write $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$. A character is a homomorphism of group schemes to $\mathbf G_m$. Let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots determined by $B$, namely the nonzero characters occurring in the adjoint $T$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$; the latter is the tangent module at the identity, defined by dual-number points reducing to the identity. In the character lattice $X^*(T)$, addition means multiplication of character values. There exist a character $\rho$ with $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$ and an extension $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$. For every such choice define the actual modules as follows. This radical is the subgroup whose geometric fibres are the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroups; unipotent means that all geometric points become unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. For every integer $m\ge1$, put $$W_m=\{f\in A[H]:f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m f(g)\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }C,\ g\in H(C),\ b\in B(C)\}.$$ Evaluation of $f$ means pullback of the regular function along its $C$-point. Use the left-translation action $(h f)(g)=f(h^{-1}g)$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with an $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ is the coordinate Hopf algebra. Its invariants are $M^H=\{x:\rho_M(x)=x\otimes1\}$. Equivariant maps commute with coactions; tensor products have diagonal coaction. These identities are tested after every commutative $A$-algebra extension, not just on $A$-points. For every $m\ge1$, left translation gives $W_m$ a rational $H$-module structure, and its underlying $A$-module is finite free of positive rank. Here finite free of positive rank means admitting a basis indexed by a finite nonempty set.

proof.text: The DVR $A$ is a PID, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Apply [lem-sfb-local-borel-quotient-geometry] to the given pair: semisimple geometric fibres are reductive, by [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable], a connected normal smooth unipotent subgroup is solvable. It gives $B=T\ltimes U$, $p:B\to T$, and the proper flag torsor $\pi:H\to Q$. Identify $T$ with $\mathbf G_m^r$. Its characters are the monomials with integer exponents: the group-like elements of $A[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ are single monomials, since coefficient comparison in $\Delta(f)=f\otimes f$ makes their coefficients orthogonal idempotents and $A$ is local. Thus restriction $X^*(T)\to X^*(T_\kappa)$ is an isomorphism. The cited geometry identifies the positive roots in this lattice with those on the closed fibre. Apply [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules] to the semisimple simply connected group $H_\kappa$; its half-sum character lifts uniquely to $\rho$ on $T$, and $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$ because restriction is injective. Set $\widetilde\rho=\rho\circ p$. Any extension trivial on $U$ equals this one by $B=T\ltimes U$.

proof.text: Fix $m\ge1$ and write $\psi=\widetilde\rho^m$. On the torsor overlap $H\times_QH=H\times_AB$, descend the trivial line on $H$ with multiplier $\psi(b)$ from $g$ to $gb$. The cocycle equation is $\psi(bb')=\psi(b)\psi(b')$. By [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] this is effective and descends to an invertible quasi-coherent sheaf $L$ on $Q$. By [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent-fpqc-sections], a section of this line is exactly a regular function satisfying $f(gb)=\psi(b)f(g)$ on the overlap. Consequently the pullback-and-trivialization map identifies $\Gamma(Q,L)$ with the actual submodule $W_m$ of the question, with the positive exponent as written. The identities are scheme identities: testing the universal point of the affine scheme $H\times_AB$ gives equality of regular functions, and conversely such equality pulls back along every algebra-valued point.

proof.text: The scheme $Q$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The invertible sheaf $L$ is coherent: on an affine trivializing open $\operatorname{Spec}D$ its sections are $D$; kernels of maps from finite free modules to $D$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], since $D$ is Noetherian. This is the local coherent-module condition. Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] to the proper map $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $L$. Its affine-base clause gives finite generation of $\Gamma(Q,L)$ over $A$, hence of $W_m$.

proof.text: Put $R=A[H]$ and $D=A[B]$. Smoothness of $H/A$ implies flatness by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], and the affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $R$ a flat $A$-module. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], $R$ is torsion-free. Its submodule $W_m$ is torsion-free as well: $aw=0$ in $W_m$ implies $aw=0$ in $R$ and hence $w=0$ for $a\ne0$. Finite generation from Step 3 now permits [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free], so $W_m$ is finite free. This step does not assert that reduction of invariants modulo the maximal ideal is exact.

proof.text:
The regular right action $r:H\times_AB\to H$ gives the $A$-linear difference map
$$d:R\to R\otimes_AD,\qquad d(f)=r^*f-f\otimes\psi.$$
Here $\psi\in D^\times$ is the character's regular function. Universal affine points identify $W_m=\ker d$. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and let $E$ be an algebraic closure of $K$. First tensor the exact sequence $0\to W_m\to R\xrightarrow{d}R\otimes_AD$ with $K$, then tensor over $K$ with $E$. These operations preserve the kernel by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]: $K$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] and $E$ is flat over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. On affine coordinate algebras these tensors are the coordinate algebras and right-action map of $H_E,B_E$. By the base compatibility and positive-root assertion of [lem-sfb-local-borel-quotient-geometry], $\rho_E$ is the half-sum for the chosen Borel. Thus $W_m\otimes_AE$ is exactly the module of [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules] for $H_E$ and is nonzero. A zero $W_m$ would have zero tensor product, so $W_m\ne0$. In a finite free module a basis indexed by the empty set gives the zero module; hence the basis in Step 4 is nonempty.

proof.text:
Define $c:R\to R\otimes_AR$ by pullback along $H\times_AH\to H$, $(g,h)\mapsto h^{-1}g$, with $g$ the function variable and $h$ the acting variable. For $w\in W_m$,
$$w(h^{-1}gb)=\psi(b)w(h^{-1}g),$$
so $(d\otimes1)c(w)=0$, after the indicated ordering of tensor factors. Since the second $R$ is flat by Step 4, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies $\ker(d\otimes1)$ with $W_m\otimes_AR$ inside $R\otimes_AR$. Therefore $c$ restricts to an $A$-linear map $c_m:W_m\to W_m\otimes_AR$. Evaluation at $h=1$ gives its counit identity. For the coassociativity identity the two pullbacks at $(g,h,k)$ both give $w((hk)^{-1}g)=w(k^{-1}h^{-1}g)$, so they agree already as functions on $H^3$. The inclusions of $W_m$ into $R$ remain injective after tensoring with one or two copies of the flat module $R$, again by the cited exactness result, so these identities in $R$ restrict to the identities in $W_m$. This is the required rational coaction, and its point formula is precisely $(h w)(g)=w(h^{-1}g)$. All these calculations are regular-function identities on affine products and therefore hold after every commutative $A$-algebra extension.
